item.text: {"summary":"Draft is broadly coherent, but the resolver/source fields do not match the canonical ledger source binding and the interval method rests on a very thin volatility sample.","requiredFixes":[{"rubricItem":"resolver","severity":"blocking","summary":"Draft resolutionSourceUrl points to the Federal Reserve current G.19 page, while the ledger contract binds first-print resolution to ALFRED/FRED sourceUrl https://alfred.stlouisfed.org/graph/alfredgraph.csv?id=NONREVSLAR with allowedHosts [\"alfred.stlouisfed.org\"].","actionRequested":"Align the JSON resolver/source fields with the ledger sourceBinding, or explicitly state the discrepancy while keeping the same slug/dataPointId/target contract."},{"rubricItem":"interval","severity":"warning","summary":"The 80% interval is based only on five 2026 monthly observations, which is too short to establish realized volatility for a noisy monthly annualized series.","actionRequested":"Use a longer same-series historical volatility sample, or explicitly justify why the Jan-May 2026 sample is the intended uncertainty basis and widen/add caveat if needed."},{"rubricItem":"model_prior","severity":"warning","summary":"The draft uses a persistence prior but does not clearly say whether a formal time-series/model prior was used or ruled out.","actionRequested":"Add one sentence that names the model prior as simple recent-mean persistence, or says a formal AR/time-series model was ruled out and why."}],"optionalSuggestions":["Clarify whether the 2025 annual nonrevolving rate is being used as a weak anchor or only as context.","Keep the tail scenarios tied to specific G.19 components such as auto credit, student-loan/federal-holder flows, and paydowns."]}
